To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

“Naso-axial line (Nax) is a reliable preoperative indicator of the maximal extent (inferior dissection) of transnasal approach to the craniovertebral joint (CVJ), and Palatine Inferio dental Arch line (PDA) is a reliable indicator of the maximal superior dissection for transoral approach.
the transoral approach has a superior exposure of the CV junction than the transnasal one.
we found that the radiological and the “effective” transoral surgical line are closer than the radiological and “effective” transnasal surgical line.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the surgical and radiological endoscopic exposure domains of the CVJ, with the aim to define reliable preoperative predictors for the transoral and the transnasal approaches.

the surgical reliability of radiological lines to predict preoperatically the maximal superior extension for the transoral route and the maximal inferior extension for the transnasals route to the craniovertebral region.

the surgical reliability and the surgical predictability of the radiological endoscopic angular domains of the transnasal and trans oral routes to the CVJ, and we found that the surgical reliability and predictability of the surgical endoscopic angular domains is significantly higher for the transoral route compared to the transnasal route.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the surgical Palatine Inferiore dental Arch line will represent the maximal extent of the superior dissection for transoral approach with a simple lateral head X-rays examination of the craniovertebral joint by open mouth; the radiological Mandibulopalatal line will represent the preoperatively calculated maximal superior extent of the transoral dissection; the Nasoaxial line will represent the radiological predictor of the maximal inferior extent of the transnasal dissection.
, in the hands of an experienced endoscopic surgeon, the transnasal route is superior to the transoral approach in terms of surgical exposition angle and working channel volume.

the surgical Palatine Inferor dental arch line will draw the maximum extent of superior dissession for the transoral endoscopic approach to the anterior CVJ with a simple lateral pre-operative radiological study.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have found a radiological line that can predict the surgical line in the transoral approach.
we have found a radiological line that can be easily calculated preoperatively and that predicts the maximal superior extent of the transoral dissection of the CVJ.
the radiological lines are useful predictors of the maximal extent for both the transnasal and trans-oral approaches.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the surgical palatine inferior dental arch line will draw the maximum extent of superior dis section for the transoral endoscopic approach.
the transoral route to the craniovertebral region is limited by the palatal arch and the superior extent of the transoral dissection cannot be extended beyond this anatomical limit.
we found a simple and reliable way to predict the maximal extent of dissection of both the approaches.
